svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Two circuits, each with a 3.0 V cell and two identical lamps. The switches are open: no current flows."], [2, "Close the switches. Conventional current flows from the + terminal, round the circuit, back to the \u2212 terminal."], [4, "Series: there is only one path, so the current is the same at every point (0.20 A on every ammeter)."], [6, "Series: the 3.0 V is shared between the lamps (1.5 V each), so they are dim. If one lamp breaks, both go out."], [8, "Parallel: each lamp is connected directly across the cell, so each gets the full 3.0 V and is brighter."], [10, "Parallel: the branch currents add up to the total current: 0.25 A + 0.25 A = 0.50 A. Each branch works on its own."]]
svg.title: Series and parallel circuits
svg.desc: Circuit diagrams with standard symbols. Series: cell, switch, two lamps and ammeters in one loop, the same current everywhere and the voltage shared. Parallel: two lamps in separate branches, each with the full voltage, branch currents adding to the total.
svg.text: Standard circuit symbols. Arrows show conventional current (+ to −). Readings for identical lamps; simple model.

g.data-info: The long line is the positive terminal, the short line the negative. Conventional current flows out of + round the circuit to −.
Open: a gap, no current. Closed: the circuit is complete and current flows.
Measures current in amperes (A). Connected in series, so the current flows through it.
Identical lamps. Brightness depends on the power: the p.d. across the lamp × the current through it.
Measures current in amperes (A). Connected in series, so the current flows through it.
Measures potential difference (p.d.) in volts (V). Connected in parallel, across the component.
Shown by arrows from + to −. Electrons actually flow the other way, from − to +.
The long line is the positive terminal, the short line the negative. Conventional current flows out of + round the circuit to −.
Open: a gap, no current. Closed: the circuit is complete and current flows.
Measures current in amperes (A). Connected in series, so the current flows through it.
Identical lamps. Brightness depends on the power: the p.d. across the lamp × the current through it.
Measures current in amperes (A). Connected in series, so the current flows through it.
Measures potential difference (p.d.) in volts (V). Connected in parallel, across the component.
Where the circuit splits or joins. Current in = current out (charge is conserved).
Shown by arrows from + to −. Electrons actually flow the other way, from − to +.

g.text: Series: I is the same everywhere · V₁ + V₂ = 1.5 V + 1.5 V = 3.0 V
Parallel: I = I₁ + I₂ = 0.25 A + 0.25 A = 0.50 A · each lamp 3.0 V
Parallel lamps are brighter: each has the full 3.0 V. In homes, lights and sockets are wired in parallel.
